Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The present petition has been filed U/s 166 & 140 M.V.Act seeking compensation of Rs.
40,00,000/- alongwith interest @24% per annum from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization on account of injuries suffered by petitioner Sh. Anil Kumar (aged 48 years) in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 18.06.2019.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 18.06.2019, injured Anil Kumar was walking on foot in gali, 25 Futa Road, Mukundpur Part II,
Delhi.

At about 11:00 PM, MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 while he was walking, offending vehicle i.e. Motorcycle bearing registration no. DL8S-CM-9756 which was being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein) at a very high speed, in a zigzag manner, came and hit against the petitioner with a great force, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to LNJP Hospital, Delhi and thereafter, he was referred to Trauma Centre and remained admitted there from 18.06.2019 to 02.07.2019.
A case U/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Bhalswa Dairy, vide FIR No. 0354/19 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioner has claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was duly insured with respondent no. 3/ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd., at the time of accident in question.

He further deposed that the petitioner was walking on foot in gali, 25 Futa Road, Mukundpur, Delhi and suddenly the respondent no. 1 came from Pragati Enclave side alongwith his motorcycle no. DL8S-CM-9756, Splendor in zigzag manner with high speed at about 11:00 pm and hit the petitioner and thereafter, the respondent no. 1/driver also fell down alongwith his bike and they caught hold the driver on the spot.

sentences.text: 14. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/1 colly) of injured prepared at Lok Nayak Hospital, shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 18.06.2019 at 11:55 PM with alleged history of RTA.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.

The petitioner was thereafter shifted to Sushruta Trauma Centre on 18.06.2019, where he MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 remained hospitalized till 22.06.2019 and again hospitalized from 28.06.2019 till 02.07.2019.
There is no opinion of Expert regarding the nature of injury being grievous or simple, from Lok Nayak Hospital and Shushruta Trauma Centre.
It is further perused that as per the Discharge Summary of Sushruta Trauma Centre, the injuries suffered by the injured were closed fracture both bone leg (left) and ORIF with ILN was done.
Again, there is no medical findings on the nature/gravity of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
Considering the entirety of the medical treatment record and the fact that petitioner has suffered fracture and surgery was also done, it is reasonable to consider the nature of injury as 'grievous'.
There is no challenge to the medical documents from the side of respondents, including insurance company.

15. There is no merit in the contention raised on behalf of respondent no. 3 that testimony of PW1 is liable to be discarded on the ground that FIR in the present case was registered on 20.06.2019 i.e.
after 2 days from the date of accident.
No doubt, accident had occurred on 18.06.2019 and FIR in the present case, was registered on 20.06.2019 i.e. after about 2 days from the date of accident.
However, the petitioner has furnished explanation for delay in lodging the FIR in his statement itself, which led to the registration of the FIR.

The contents of FIR would show that the petitioner clearly mentioned therein the reason for delay in lodging of FIR that he could not get the FIR lodged on time as he was not in position to give statement due to acute pain in his leg.

Even otherwise DD No. 084A MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 regarding the accident was recorded at PS. Bhalswa Dairy on the date of accident itself i.e. 18.06.2019.
16.
It is relevant to note that none of the respondents cross-examined PW1 regarding the explanation for delay in registration of FIR.
Moreover, the MLC of the petitioner/injured is of the same day of accident i.e. 18.06.2019 showing therein alleged history of RTA.

Apart from this, Ld.
Counsel for insurance company himself gave suggestion to the petitioner that the accident had taken place due to his negligence as he suddenly came in front of the motorcycle of respondent no. 1 or that accident had occurred due to the negligence of petitioner himself which shows that insurance company admitted the accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the accident in question.

sentences.text: In the aforesaid facts and circumstances where the cogent explanation has been furnished about the delay in the registration of FIR in criminal case, same can not be considered to be fatal for the case of claimant in present proceedings.

Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.

While saying so, I am fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter titled as "Ravi Vs. Badri Narayan & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 18.02.2011.

19. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

20. It has been duly established that petitioner sustained injuries in the road accident which took place on 18.06.2019 at about 11:00 PM in gali, 25 Futa Road, Mukundpur Part II, Delhi, as per his MLC and treatment record duly proved, in the said road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no. 1/driver.
MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 21.

The intent and objective of the Beneficial Legislation is to grant equitable compensation to the vulnerable victims of road accidents and dynamic law has evolved towards grant of just and fair quantum of awards and has brought consistency and uniformity towards the desired goal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009) 6 SCC 121, which was affirmed by a bench of three Honble Judges in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr.,
(2013) 9 SCC 65, held as under:
"16.

sentences.text: "Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit.

sentences.text: Assessment of compensation though involving certain hypothetical considerations, should nevertheless be objective.
Justice and justness emanate from equality in treatment, consistency and thoroughness in adjudication, and fairness and uniformity in the decision making process and the decisions.
While it may not be possible to have mathematical precision or identical awards, in assessing compensation, same or similar facts should lead to awards in the same range.

When the factors/inputs are the same, and the formula/legal principles are the same,
consistency and uniformity, and not divergence and freakiness, should be the result of adjudication to arrive at just compensation..."
22.

These guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" have been torch bearer in injury cases also as laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 Insurance Co,.
Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors, wherein it has been held:-
"10.
The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.
Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages....."

11. The general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".
23.

The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

MEDICAL EXPENSES 25.

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit(Ex. PW1/A) that after the accident, he was taken to Lok Nayak Hospital, Delhi, where he was medically examined and thereafter, he was referred to Sushruta Trauma Centre, where he remained admitted from 18.06.2019 to 22.06.2019 and from 28.06.2019 to 02.07.2019.
He further deposed that he had sustained grievous injury i.e. closed fracture both bone left leg and other multiple injuries in the accident.
He further deposed that he had already spent more than Rs. 1 lakh on his treatment.
For this, he has relied upon medical bills Ex. PW1/3(colly).
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he did not have any mediclaim policy.
He denied the suggestion that he was fully cured after his treatment in Trauma Centre.
He further denied the suggestion that the bills filed by him were forged and fabricated.
He admitted that the Trauma Centre was a MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 government hospital and the free treatment was given to him in the hospital.
He deposed that the bill dated 06.06.2021 pertained to removal of rod.
He further deposed that the doctor prescribed the medicines for 16 days only.
He denied the suggestion that bill dated 23.06.2019 and 23.07.2019 were forged and fabricated.
He admitted that no prescription for these bills were filed on record.
He denied the suggestion that he had not spent Rs. 1,00,000/- on his treatment.
26. It is relevant to note that the injured has relied upon medical bills(Ex. PW1/3 colly) to the tune of Rs. 72,471/- only.
It is quite evident that the respondents have not disputed the authenticity and genuineness of the said medical bills during the course of inquiry.
They have also not led any evidence in rebuttal so as to create any doubt on the genuineness of said bills.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs. 72,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

sentences.text: 28. During the course of arguments, Ld. Counsel for injured argued that due to the injuries suffered by him, he could not work for considerable period and thus, he has suffered loss of income and as such, appropriate compensation shall be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
29. The treatment record (which is part of Ex. PW1/3 colly) of petitioner shows that he had suffered closed fracture both bone leg (left) and ORIF with ILN was done.
As per discharge summary of Sushruta Trauma Centre, Delhi, petitioner was admitted in the aforesaid hospital on 18.06.2019 and was discharged on 22.06.2019.
As per another discharge summary of Sushruta Trauma Centre, the petitioner was again admitted in the said hospital on 28.06.2019 and was discharged on 02.07.2019.

The petitioner has MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 not filed any document in order to show till what period he had received treatment for the injuries suffered by him in the accident in question.
However, treatment record relied upon by the petitioner shows that he had received treatment from different hospitals on different occasions.
It may be noted here that the case of petitioner was interlock nailing and the same was done on 20.06.2019.
As per discharge sheet of Divine Multispeciality Hospital & Cancer Centre, another surgery of petitioner was done on 05.06.2021 for implant removal left tibia.

In the absence of any definite evidence being brought on record showing the actual period till which the petitioner had received medical treatment for the injuries sustained by him due to accident in question, it would necessarily involve some guess in assessing the loss of income.
It can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained closed fracture both bone leg (left) as mentioned above due to the accident.
This fact is duly corroborated by the medical treatment record filed by the petitioner.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work atleast for a period of 1 year or so.
30. It may be noted here that no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove monthly income of injured/petitioner at the time of accident in question.
However, the petitioner has filed his educational qualification documents i.e. 10th class marksheet and 12th class marksheet Ex. PW1/4 and Ex. PW1/5 respectively.

Thus, his loss of income has to be assessed while taking the income of a Matrriculate person under Minimum MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 Wages Act applicable during the period in question.
The minimum wages of a matriculate person were Rs. 17,508/- per month as on the date of accident which is 18.06.2019.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 2,10,000/- (rounded off) (Rs. 17,508/- x 12) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, I find substance in the plea raised on behalf of insurance company that for want of valid and effective driving licence in favour of respondent no. 1 being proved on record, it would be termed as breach in the terms and conditions of insurance policy.
This brings me down to the next question as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.

It is apparent on record that respondent no. 2 is the registered owner of offending vehicle at the time of accident and respondent no. 1 is the son of respondent no. 2 who allowed him to drive the offending vehicle despite knowing the fact that respondent no. 1 is not authorize to drive the offending vehicle being minor and was not holding the driving licence at the time of accident.
It was the duty of registered owner to see who was driving her vehicle whether he was having valid and effective driving licence at that time or not.

In the present case, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries because the respondent no. 2 did not take appropriate steps to ensure that his vehicle was being driven only by a person holding valid driving licence.

The respondent no.
2 also failed to appear before this Tribunal and she preferred to stay away from the proceedings of the present case.

Thus, insurance company is entitled to recovery rights against respondent no.
2/registered owner.

While taking this MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD:

IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.", MAC. APP. 24/2023, decided on 06.02.2018,
whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has been pleased to observed as under:-
xxxxx " Once the appellant, despite being aware that his son was a minor child, left the keys of his car at home and has failed to give any explanation as to why the keys of the car at home were left unattended when he himself was not there, the defence being taken by the appellant is apparently an afterthought in an attempt to somehow to escape his liability.

sentences.text: Even otherwise, the appellant did not lead any independent witness in support of his plea that the car was being driven by his minor son without his knowledge and permission.

8.I may also note that as observed by the learned Tribunal, this plea of his minor son having taken the car without his permission, was not even taken by the appellant either before the concerned police authority or the Juvenile Justice Board.

In a matter like this, when the parents of minor children permit him/her to drive a motor vehicle, not only they put the lives of their own children in danger but also endager the life of common citizens.

In the present case,the deceased Mr. Harinder Kumar, a young man of 42 years lost his life only because the appellant did not take appropriate steps to ensure that his vehicle is driven only by a person holding a valid driving licence.

This Court, therefore, cannot condone such an act of the appellant and fasten the MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD:
01.10.2024 liability on the insurance company when it is evident that the terms of the insurance policy were breached by the appellant himself"

Even otherwise, it is well settled law that delay in lodging FIR can not be a ground to throw away the case of claimant in such like proceedings in the backdrop of the conditions prevailing in our society where one can not expect common man to rush to police station for registration of FIR immediately after the accident.
While saying so, I am fortified by the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter titled as "Ravi Vs. Badri Narayan & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on MACP No. 576/19; FIR No. 354/19; PS. Bhalswa Dairy DOD: 01.10.2024 18.02.2011.

23.
The Hon'ble Apex Court, in further development of the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation, has pronounced guiding parameters that "the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
